decisions.decision: Per the town's existing agreement with consultant Community Scale, the planning board will bring exactly one zoning option to town meeting, not multiple options.
Residents were asked to submit any further questions or feedback in writing on note cards before leaving, to be passed to the planning board.
The moderator tabled further discussion of opposition to the state mandate itself in order to focus remaining time on which zoning option to recommend.

minutes.headline: Planning Board leans toward Tritown 'paper compliance' to meet the state's MBTA Communities housing mandate
minutes.summary: This was a public input session, not a voting meeting: the planning board chair presented the MBTA Communities zoning mandate, the four candidate sites (White Street, Tritown, Rogers Way, Leominster Shirley Road), and four possible compliance paths, then took extensive resident questions and comments. No formal vote occurred; the chair reiterated that the planning board will bring one bylaw option to a November special town meeting, and many residents and the chair himself leaned toward 'paper compliance' using Tritown's existing zoning while reserving Leominster Shirley Road for a locally designed mixed-use development.

what_happened.line: Planning board will bring exactly one MBTA Communities zoning option to a November special town meeting, per its consultant agreement.
No vote was taken; this was a public input session, and the chair and many residents leaned toward 'paper compliance' using Tritown's existing zoning.
That approach would reserve Leominster Shirley Road for a separately, locally designed mixed-use development rather than for MBTA compliance.
Residents pressed unresolved questions about school enrollment, water and sewer capacity, and who any new housing would actually serve.

why_it_matters: This shapes the single zoning bylaw residents will be asked to vote on at the November special town meeting, and which sites see new housing capacity.
A 'paper compliance' approach would meet the state mandate largely on paper, without necessarily adding housing units, according to several residents at the meeting.
Water, sewer and school-capacity questions raised here were not answered in this session and remain open going into that vote.
